Vessel area is about 24 × 24 × 0.85 ≈ 490 cm², but the apple is the only food, so the plate area matters only for the percentage.

**STEP 3 - Items:** One whole apple. A few tiny yellowish residue specks sit on the plate, but they are negligible and not counted.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** 50 cm² × ~7 cm height ≈ 350 ml (outer envelope).

**STEP 6 - Grams:** 350 ml × 0.6 g/ml ≈ 210 g. Cross-check: a medium apple typically weighs about 180 to 200 g, so I use about 190 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Raw apple is about 52 kcal/100 g. 190 g × 0.52 ≈ 99 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** One medium apple at about 190 g and about 100 kcal is plausible for what is visible. The plate is only about 10% covered, which fits a single apple, not a full meal.

**Estimate:** about 190 g of apple, about 100 kcal.
